ns2:course.label: New Modernities South
ns2:course.description: Examination of how nonwestern societies, such as Japan, China, India, the Islamic world, Africa and Latin America, analyze their modernity. The study of modernity and the idea of multiple modernities by combining and contrasting western and nonwestern views of modernity, postmodernism and capitalism. 3 undergraduate hours. 4 graduate hours. Prerequisite: Introductory course in social science or SOC 100 or consent of instructor.
